chokh/rx3 is the zebrafish ortholog of RAX (retina and anterior neural fold homeobox). Loss of eyes caused by rx3 mutation is a primary characterization of RAX gene function in eye formation, directly relevant to both the RAX and RAX2 gene entries and the ocular malformations topic.

Autosomal dominant Axenfeld-Rieger anomaly mapped to 6p25, the locus of FOXC1 (forkhead box C1). This is a foundational genetic mapping study for FOXC1-associated anterior segment disease. Directly relevant to both FOXC1 gene entry and ocular malformations.

The Small eye (Sey) mouse is the canonical PAX6 animal model and central to ophthalmogenetics research on PAX6. While the paper's focus is on cortical neuronal migration defects (a non-ocular phenotype), it characterizes the fundamental PAX6 mutation model and the gene link is direct. For a gene-centric library, understanding PAX6 mutation phenotypes across tissues is part of its biology; the ophthalmogenetics connection is plausible.
